cells.tense: You're here with the pen down, and others can borrow the steadiness you keep.
cells.act: hold many truths at once without collapsing them
cells.ask: Keep two things in view at once with someone close — what you need and what they need — and stand in both without making either one lose.
cells.core:
You can say what a thing is and mean it, where you stand, what you expect, what isn't okay, and say it so the other person stays near rather than leaving. It lands as clear, not sharp, and the two of you come away closer. What you declare, you declare for both sides.

When you talk with someone close, put the shape of what is between you into words plainly. Then keep two of their truths next to your own without flattening either, and step forward on one. Offer it instead of handing it down. That is how you stay direct without shutting the other person out.
cells.sheetLine: You can say the shape and stay in step.
cells.verb: declaring the shape of a thing so the people in it can meet

cells.tense: You're already saying where things will land before anyone has spoken.
cells.act: read the hardest page of it twice, slowly, before you stop
cells.ask: Read the hardest part of what someone close said twice, slowly, and stay with it a while before you answer them.
cells.core:
You want the ground laid before the conversation starts. You say where things will land, what people will do with it, before they've said anything. And the more you talk it into shape ahead of time, the more the other person is left holding a version they didn't write. It keeps you ahead of them, and further from them.

So before you answer someone close, read the hardest part of what they said twice, slowly, and stay with it a while. Depth is already yours; putting it under their words instead of over them is what turns the declaration into something that connects. Under your feet, you can stand on it. Over their head, they can't reach you.

cells.tense: You're standing at the threshold of what you meant to carry, long after it would have been welcome.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Do today's small part of rebuilding with someone you've let drift: the call, the message, the showing up you've been steering around.
cells.core:
Something between you and someone else hasn't been carried forward, and it's been a while. You may have told yourself the moment passed, or that it isn't yours to start. So the connection sits where it was, and the hours go by. That keeping still is the whole posture, and nothing new is being built under it.

Give one small part of it today. Not the whole conversation, just the next piece that keeps it from going dead: the call, the message, the showing up somewhere you've been avoiding. That's how a structure gets built back, one day's part at a time, before you can see how it turns out.

cells.tense: You're holding the shape of the room without saying that you made it hold.
cells.act: take in the yield of what was transformed
cells.ask: Name to yourself one thing a change grew, before you tidy it into a cleaner account of it.
cells.core:
You keep the space between people steady. When a conversation could go badly, you shape it so it goes well, and the ease looks like something that simply happened. That is real work, and it holds: reading the room, saying the right thing at the right time, letting the other person finish. They come away aligned, and often don't see why.

Some of what you've been holding came out of something that changed. Let what it grew sit with you first, without sorting it into a story. When you can name it to yourself as the work it was, the care that holds the room stays yours. Then the order around you is something you are making, not something that just happens near you.
